### T4.7 — Retire legacy `PluginBuilder` `[L]`
- **Change:** migrate core plugins to `definePlugin` one-by-one (email first, done in T3.6); make `PluginBuilder` a thin shim that calls `definePlugin`; remove only once no core plugin (`workflow-plugin`, etc.) depends on it.

**Phase 4 exit (FUTURE-PROOF):** clean tree, single type identity, build-time distribution, versioning gate, dogfooded reference app, retiring legacy SDK.

## Suggested sequencing & parallelism

- **Sprint 1 (start now):** Phase 1 entirely (T1.1→T1.6; T1.3–T1.6 parallelize after T1.1/T1.2 land the catalog). → extend #844, merge.
- **Sprint 2:** Phase 2 (T2.1–T2.3 dispatch in parallel; T2.4 after Phase 1 names; T2.5–T2.7 parallel). → new PR.
- **Sprint 3:** Phase 3 (T3.2 `bootIsolate` is the critical path; T3.1/T3.4/T3.6 parallel). → **production-ready** PR.
- **Sprint 4+:** Phase 4 (T4.1 first — unblocks type tightening; rest parallel). → future-proof.

**Critical path:** T1.2 (catalog names) → T2.4 (gate keys off names) and T3.2 (`bootIsolate`) → T3.3 (cron). Everything else fans off these.

## Definition of done (every task)
1. Core unit + integration suite green (`npm test --workspace=@sonicjs-cms/core`).
2. `tsc --noEmit` clean; `eslint src/` 0 errors.
3. New behavior has a unit **and** (if user-visible) integration test; breaking catalog/cap changes have alias + deprecation-warn tests.
4. Verified live in `my-sonicjs-app` where it touches a request/cron path.
5. Cross-checked against the Infowall reference for any "port" task.

## Risks carried from the analysis
- **Breaking the shipped catalog** (T1.2): mitigated by the one-release alias window + same-change test updates.
- **`bootIsolate` is a real refactor** (T3.2), not a one-liner — both `initEmailService` and the wire trigger are closures inside `createSonicJSApp` today.
- **Reconciliation is non-portable** (T3.5): Infowall's CF-GraphQL reconciler can't be copied; per-provider `reconcile()` is net-new; `delivery_state` stays null for providers without delivery webhooks.
- **Reference-app drift** (T4.6): breaking changes won't surface in `my-sonicjs-app` until it dogfoods the framework.

| **T2.2** | `plugins/available/magic-link-auth/index.ts`, `plugins/core-plugins/otp-login-plugin/index.ts` | `auth:magic-link:consumed` on successful verify; `auth:otp:verified` on OTP verify |
| **T2.3** | `routes/api-content-crud.ts` | `content:before:create/update/delete` (in-band, payload mutations flow through to DB write); `content:after:create/update/delete` + `content:after:publish` (fire-and-forget); `content:read` (fire-and-forget) |
| **T2.4** | `plugins/capabilities.ts` (`HOOK_CAPABILITY_MAP`), `plugins/wire.ts` | Wire Phase A now gates declarative hook subscriptions by required capability; v3 plugins gated, old PluginBuilder plugins exempt; non-strict warns, strict records SonicCapabilityError |

| **T2.6** | `__tests__/plugins/no-event-without-dispatch-site.test.ts` | CI guard: every HOOK_EVENT_NAMES entry must have a `dispatchHookEvent()` call in source |
| **T2.7** | `__tests__/plugins/wire-integration.test.ts` | Rewired to call `dispatchHookEvent()` (same helper production routes use) instead of manually calling `hooks.dispatch()` |

### Key design decisions
- `dispatchHookEvent(c, event, payload, mode)` takes the Hono context and safely extracts `executionCtx` (it's absent in Node test environments — Hono throws on access).
- Cancel semantics: the underlying `HookSystemImpl` swallows non-CRITICAL errors. Hard-cancel requires `throw new Error('CRITICAL: ...')`. Full soft-cancel is a Phase 3 hook-system upgrade.
- `content:before:*` mutations: the returned payload's `data` map is applied to the DB write, so plugins can add/change fields pre-insert.

# SonicJS Plugin System Overhaul — Development Plan

Source: https://github.com/sonicjs-org/sonicjs/blob/main/PLUGIN_SYSTEM_OVERHAUL_PLAN.md

# SonicJS Plugin System Overhaul — Development Plan

> **Status:** Draft for review · **Date:** 2026-06-01 · **Branch:** `lane711/plugin-system-issues`
> **Goal:** Fix the plugin system *once and for all*. Replace the hand-wired, partially-functional v1 plugin system with a typed, two-phase, capability-aware **v3 plugin SDK** — fully backed by unit, integration, and E2E tests, and validated by migrating every core plugin onto it.

## Table of Contents

1. [Executive Summary](#1-executive-summary)
2. [Current State — What We Actually Have](#2-current-state--what-we-actually-have)
3. [The Problem, Stated Precisely](#3-the-problem-stated-precisely)
4. [Inventory: Open Issues, PRs & the Infowall v3 Proposal](#4-inventory-open-issues-prs--the-infowall-v3-proposal)
5. [Reference Deep Dive — Strapi v5](#5-reference-deep-dive--strapi-v5)
6. [Reference Deep Dive — Payload CMS v3](#6-reference-deep-dive--payload-cms-v3)
7. [Design Synthesis — What SonicJS Should Borrow](#7-design-synthesis--what-sonicjs-should-borrow)
8. [Target Architecture — SonicJS v3 Plugin SDK](#8-target-architecture--sonicjs-v3-plugin-sdk)
9. [Phased Implementation Plan](#9-phased-implementation-plan)
10. [Testing Strategy](#10-testing-strategy)
11. [Core Plugin Migration Plan](#11-core-plugin-migration-plan)
12. [Issue Traceability Matrix](#12-issue-traceability-matrix)
13. [Risks & Open Questions](#13-risks--open-questions)

## 1. Executive Summary

SonicJS ships a plugin **SDK** (`PluginBuilder`, hook system, plugin registry, DB-backed plugin tables, admin UI) that is *architecturally sound but incomplete in execution*. The single load-bearing defect: **plugins declare routes/middleware/hooks, but nothing generically mounts them into the running Hono app.** Every core plugin is instead hand-wired in `packages/core/src/app.ts`, each with a comment warning it "MUST be registered BEFORE `/admin/plugins`." Community plugins, scaffolded apps, and any plugin relying on `PluginBuilder.addRoute()` silently 404.

This single defect is the root cause of, or directly related to, most of the open plugin issues (#758, #621, #829, #834) and is exactly what the **Infowall v3 plugin architecture** (the May 2026 progress doc) solved in a sister fork. That fork proved — empirically, with 2,824 passing tests — a clean model: **synchronous `register(app)` at construction time, asynchronous `wireRegisteredPlugins()` on first request**, with capability-gated context, typed hook subscriptions, cron declarations, and singleton services.

This plan adopts that model for SonicJS, cross-checks it against how **Strapi** and **Payload** solve the same problems, and lays out a phased, test-first rollout: build the SDK core, fix mounting, migrate all ~22 core plugins onto the new pattern (email first, as the reference), and back the whole thing with real unit + integration + E2E coverage.

## 2. Current State — What We Actually Have

All paths below are under `packages/core/src/` unless noted. Verified against branch `lane711/plugin-system-issues`.

### 2.1 The pieces that exist

| Subsystem | File(s) | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Plugin type & interface | `plugins/types.ts` (1–439) | ✅ Defined |
| Fluent builder SDK | `plugins/sdk/plugin-builder.ts` | ✅ `addRoute/addMiddleware/addModel/addService/addAdminPage/addHook/lifecycle` |
| Plugin manager (lifecycle orchestrator) | `plugins/plugin-manager.ts` (1–423) | ⚠️ Collects routes into a `Map` but never mounts them |
| Plugin registry (storage, dep resolution) | `plugins/plugin-registry.ts` | ✅ Circular-dep detection, load-order resolution |
| Hook system | `plugins/hook-system.ts` (1–289) | ✅ Priority ordering, scoped per-plugin, `execute()` with cancellation |
| Plugin validator | `plugins/plugin-validator.ts` | ✅ Validates shape/deps |
| Manifest registry (auto-generated) | `plugins/manifest-registry.ts` | ✅ Generated by `packages/scripts/generate-plugin-registry.mjs` |

| Tests | `__tests__/plugins/plugin-builder*.test.ts`, `__tests__/routes/admin-plugins.test.ts`, `tests/e2e/15,21,28,29,38,39,40,43-*.spec.ts` | ⚠️ Builder + UI covered; mounting/hooks/lifecycle integration **not** covered |

### 2.2 The `Plugin` interface (today)

```ts
interface Plugin {
  name: string; version: string; description?: string
  author?: { name; email; url }; dependencies?: string[]
  compatibility?: string; license?: string
  routes?: PluginRoutes[]; middleware?: PluginMiddleware[]
  models?: PluginModel[]; services?: PluginService[]
  adminPages?: PluginAdminPage[]; adminComponents?: PluginComponent[]
  menuItems?: PluginMenuItem[]; hooks?: PluginHook[]
  install?(ctx): Promise<void>; uninstall?(ctx): Promise<void>
  activate?(ctx): Promise<void>; deactivate?(ctx): Promise<void>
  configure?(config): Promise<void>
}
```

### 2.3 How mounting *actually* works today (the smoking gun)

`app.ts` mounts every plugin **by hand**, in a strict order, each guarded by a comment:

```ts
// app.ts (excerpt, line numbers from current branch)
230  // Plugin routes - Security Audit (MUST be registered BEFORE admin/plugins to avoid route conflict)
237  // Plugin routes - AI Search (MUST be registered BEFORE admin/plugins to avoid route conflict)
249  // Plugin routes - OAuth Providers (MUST be registered BEFORE admin/plugins ...)
263  // Plugin routes - OTP Login (MUST be registered BEFORE admin/plugins ...)
271  // Plugin routes - Analytics (must be before /admin/plugins catch-all)
281  // Plugin routes - Stripe (must be before /admin/plugins catch-all)
288  app.route('/admin/plugins', adminPluginRoutes)   // ← generic plugins admin
290  app.route('/admin', adminUsersRoutes)            // ← bare /admin catch-all
```

**Consequences:**
- A plugin that *only* uses `PluginBuilder.addRoute()` (e.g. global-variables) is never mounted → 404 (**#758**).
- Scaffolded apps don't know they must hand-mount or regenerate the registry (**#621**).
- Adding a plugin means editing core `app.ts` — community plugins can't do this (**#829**, **#830**).
- Route order is positional and fragile; the `/admin` catch-all shadows anything mounted after it.

### 2.4 Honest assessment

- **Type safety:** good (TS + Zod in places).
- **Extension points declared:** good.
- **Extension points *wired*:** broken. Routes/middleware/models declared in the builder are collected but not applied generically.
- **Capability gating:** absent.
- **Cron for plugins:** absent (workflow plugin has a bespoke `scheduled_at`).
- **Typed hooks:** hooks are string-keyed; payloads are untyped.
- **Test coverage of the wiring:** absent (the exact area that's broken is the area with no integration tests).

## 3. The Problem, Stated Precisely

> **Plugins describe what they want (routes, hooks, services, crons), but the host never generically applies those descriptions, and where it does apply them it must do so by editing core source in a position-sensitive way.**

Five concrete failures fall out of that one root cause:

1. **No generic route mounting** — `addRoute()` is dead metadata for non-hardcoded plugins (#758).
2. **Position-sensitive hand-wiring** — `/admin` catch-all shadows late-mounted plugin routes; ordering is encoded as comments, not enforced.
3. **No first-class registration API for consumers** — users must edit core or hand-mount (#621, #829).
4. **No capability/permission boundary** — any plugin can do anything; no `ctx.email`-style scoping.
5. **Untyped hooks + no cron** — string hook names, untyped payloads, no scheduled-task surface.

And the meta-problem: **the broken parts have no integration/E2E coverage**, so regressions are invisible until a user hits a 404 in production.

### 4.2 The Infowall v3 plugin architecture (May 2026 progress doc)

A sister fork built and shipped a v3 plugin SDK across four PRs (PR-S1 types, PR-S2 register pipeline, PR-S3 hook-system singleton + wiring, PR-M), then migrated the **email plugin (PR-E)** as the first real consumer. Key claims, all reportedly green (2,824 tests passing, tsc clean):

- **Two-pass lifecycle:** `register(app)` (sync, mounts routes) → `onBoot` (async, wires env-dependent services after *all* plugins register).
- **Capability-gated context:** `ctx.email` throws `SonicCapabilityError` if the plugin didn't declare `email:send`. Eleven capabilities defined.
- **Typed hook subscriptions:** subscribing to `auth:registration:completed` yields the narrowed payload shape; TS rejects wrong field names at the subscribe site.
- **Cron surface:** `crons: [{ schedule: '*/15 * * * *', hookFamily: 'email-reconciliation' }]` in the manifest; an `on-cron-tick` handler filters by `event.hookFamily`.
- **Singleton services:** `email-service-singleton.ts` mirrors `hook-system-singleton.ts` (three-function API, throw-before-set), set eagerly in the app factory so cron handlers running outside HTTP context still get the service.

**The empirically-discovered bug that reshaped the design (critical for SonicJS too):**

> **Hono's SmartRouter locks after the first request.** Calling `app.route()` from inside a middleware that fires lazily on first request throws `Error: Can not add a route since the matcher is already built`.

The fix splits registration into two functions:

| Function | When | What |
|---|---|---|
| `registerPluginRoutes(app, plugins)` | **Synchronous**, at construction, inline in the app factory, **between the last core mount and the bare `/admin` catch-all** | Validate, topo-sort, call `plugin.register?.(app)` for each. Routes mount before the matcher builds and before `/admin/*` — no shadowing. |
| `wireRegisteredPlugins(ordered, byId, hostContext)` | **Async**, lazy on first request | Hook subscriptions, cron registration, `onBoot`. Needs per-request env. |

Contract: **`register()` must be synchronous**; a `Promise` return is rejected with a named error rather than hanging. Async work belongs in `onBoot`.

> **Why this matters for SonicJS directly:** SonicJS has the *exact same* `/admin` catch-all-after-plugins structure (see §2.3). Any SonicJS plugin that mounts routes lazily will hit the identical SmartRouter lock. The fix is fork-agnostic. We should align on it rather than discover it independently.

## 5. Reference Deep Dive — Strapi v5

> Verified against docs.strapi.io (v5) and `strapi/strapi` `main`.

### 5.1 The big picture
A Strapi plugin is **two independently-loaded programs sharing a name**: a *server* program (`./strapi-server` export) and an *admin* program (`./strapi-admin` export). They never share a runtime; the only contract is the plugin **id**. Everything is wired through a single mutable global `strapi` object — a **service-locator/registry**, not constructor DI. Plugins are **plain config objects, not classes** (there's still a `// TODO: validate plugin format` in the loader — no shape validation).

### 5.2 Server entry & lifecycle
```ts
// server/src/index.ts
export default () => ({ register, bootstrap, destroy, config,
  contentTypes, routes, controllers, services, policies, middlewares })
```
| Hook | Timing | Available |
|---|---|---|
| `register({ strapi })` | Before app setup — **no DB, no routes yet** | Register custom fields, content-type extensions, document-service middleware |
| `bootstrap({ strapi })` | After full setup, before HTTP listen | Everything — DB, all plugins' services, seed |
| `destroy({ strapi })` | Shutdown | Cleanup |

**Two-phase lifecycle (register → bootstrap) is the same shape Infowall's v3 uses** (register → onBoot). Strapi validates this pattern at industrial scale.

### 5.3 Discovery & registration
Three sources merged with `defaultsDeep`, filtered by `enabled`:
1. **Internal core plugins** — hardcoded, always on (`content-manager`, `upload`, `i18n`, …).
2. **npm plugins** — auto-discovered: Strapi scans `dependencies`, requires each `package.json`, keeps those with **`strapi.kind === 'plugin'`**. *No `config/plugins.js` entry needed.*
3. **Declared plugins** — `config/plugins.js`; a `resolve` path makes it a local plugin.

```js
// config/plugins.js
module.exports = ({ env }) => ({
  i18n: true,
  'my-plugin': { enabled: true, resolve: './src/plugins/my-plugin', config: { /* … */ } },
})
```

### 5.4 Extension points & namespacing
Each plugin is wrapped as a **module** under namespace `plugin::<name>` and distributed into typed registries. Accessors resolve **lazily by string at call time**:
```ts
strapi.plugin('my-plugin').service('my-service')   // plugin::my-plugin.my-service
strapi.plugin('my-plugin').controller('x')
strapi.plugin('my-plugin').contentType('thing')
strapi.plugin('my-plugin').config('key')
```
Isolation = **namespacing only**, not sandboxing. Any plugin can read/mutate any registry.

### 5.5 Three interception layers (a known footgun)
1. **Document Service middleware** (`strapi.documents.use(...)`) — v5-recommended, content-agnostic, registered in `register()`.
2. **DB/ORM lifecycle hooks** (`beforeCreate`, `afterUpdate`, … 16+ events) — *don't fire for raw Knex; bulk ops fire only the batch event.*
3. **Event hub** (`strapi.eventHub.emit/on`) — pub/sub that webhooks consume.

> **Lesson for SonicJS:** Strapi's biggest plugin footgun is *three overlapping ways to intercept*, where picking the wrong layer silently misses cases. SonicJS should expose **one** typed hook layer, not three.

### 5.6 Config validation
Per-plugin `config: { default, validator }` where `validator` is an **imperative throwing function** (not a schema). User config from `config/plugins.js` merged with per-env overrides via `defaultsDeep` (user wins).

### 5.7 Type safety — candid
Lifecycle and `config` are typed; **`services`, `policies`, `middlewares`, `registerTrads` are still `unknown`** at the entry boundary, and accessors are stringly-typed (no per-plugin service map). Malformed plugins fail late.

### 5.8 Takeaways for SonicJS
- ✅ **Two-phase lifecycle** (register/bootstrap) — adopt.
- ✅ **Auto-discovery via a `package.json` metadata key** — adopt the idea (but build-time on Workers; see §7).
- ✅ **Namespacing** for plugin-owned tables/services — adopt.
- ⚠️ **Service-locator with stringly-typed lookups** — *improve on this* with typed capabilities/services.
- ❌ **Three interception layers** — *don't* replicate; one typed hook system.

## 6. Reference Deep Dive — Payload CMS v3

> Verified against payloadcms.com/docs and `payloadcms/payload` `main` (template fetched verbatim).

### 6.1 The big picture — a plugin is a config transformer
```ts
export type Plugin = (config: Config) => Config | Promise<Config>
```
That's the **entire contract.** No register API, no lifecycle object. Real plugins are curried: `(options) => (config) => Config`. Plugins are composed as a **left-to-right fold** over the `plugins: []` array:
```
config₀ → pluginA → config₁ → pluginB → … → sanitize → init
```
Order is the *only* dependency mechanism — no `dependsOn`, no topological sort.

### 6.2 What a plugin can do
Anything the `Config` can express: push new collections/globals, locate-and-mutate existing collections' fields, add `endpoints`, merge into hook arrays, push admin component **path-strings**, register `jobs.tasks`, and **chain `onInit`**:
```ts
const prev = config.onInit
config.onInit = async (payload) => { if (prev) await prev(payload); /* seed */ }
```

### 6.3 The merge discipline (the core correctness rule)
Because every plugin folds over a shared object, the rule is **never clobber**:
- Arrays → guard `||= []`, spread, append.
- Objects → shallow-spread to preserve siblings.
- Functions (`onInit`) → capture & invoke the previous.

TypeScript guarantees *structure*, not *composition* — it won't catch a forgotten spread that drops a prior plugin's contributions.

### 6.4 The `disabled` ≠ removed insight (load-bearing)
The official template, when `disabled`, **keeps schema-affecting additions** (collections/fields) and only skips *behavioral* additions (endpoints, components, onInit). Why: schema follows config, so a toggle that dropped collections would generate a **destructive migration**.

> **Lesson for SonicJS:** a plugin's **schema contributions** and its **runtime behavior** have *different lifecycles*. Conflating enable/disable with create/drop-table is the failure mode to avoid. This directly informs how SonicJS `activate/deactivate` should (not) touch tables.

### 6.5 Hooks model — one coherent set
Four tiers, all server-only (stripped from client bundle): root (`afterError`), **collection hooks** (`beforeOperation → beforeValidate → beforeChange → afterChange → beforeRead → afterRead → beforeDelete → afterDelete → afterOperation → afterError`), **field hooks**, **global hooks**, plus auth hooks. Strongly typed and generic over the document type: `CollectionBeforeChangeHook<Post>`.

### 6.6 Jobs / queues / tasks
Built-in queue: **Task** (handler + `inputSchema`/`outputSchema` + `retries` + `schedule`), **Workflow** (ordered tasks, retry from failure point), **Job** (queued instance), **Queue** (named bucket). Execution is *decoupled from queuing* — bin script / `autoRun` cron / `GET /api/payload-jobs/run`. **A `schedule` alone runs nothing**; you need an execution mechanism. A plugin registers a task by pushing into `config.jobs.tasks`.

> **Lesson for SonicJS:** on Cloudflare Workers, the "execution mechanism" is the Cron Trigger / `scheduled()` handler. Plugin cron declarations must be *collected* and dispatched by a single `scheduled()` entry — mirroring Infowall's `on-cron-tick` filtering by `hookFamily`.

### 6.7 Admin UI extension — path-strings, not imports
RSC-based: config references components by **`package/subpath#ExportName`** strings (never imports React into the Node config), resolved via a generated **import map**.

### 6.8 Functional transformer vs. imperative register — the central tradeoff
| | Functional transformer (Payload) | Imperative register (Strapi / Infowall / proposed SonicJS) |
|---|---|---|
| API surface to maintain | None (the `Config` type *is* the API) | A register/builder API to design & version |
| Composability | Trivial fold; later plugins see earlier output | Explicit; needs ordering rules |
| Dependency resolution | Manual (array order only) | Can do topo-sort / `dependsOn` |
| Safety / scoping | None — any plugin can rewrite anything | Capabilities can scope what each plugin touches |
| Footgun | Forgetting to spread silently clobbers | Async-in-register / route-after-catch-all |
| Type safety | Structural, end-to-end | As good as the register API is designed |

### 6.9 Takeaways for SonicJS
- ✅ **Strong end-to-end types** + generated slug/document types — aspire to this.
- ✅ **`disabled` keeps schema** — adopt as the activate/deactivate rule.
- ✅ **One coherent, typed hook set** — adopt.
- ✅ **Jobs decoupled from execution; cron needs a runner** — adopt for Workers `scheduled()`.
- ⚠️ **Pure functional transformer** — *not* a fit for SonicJS (Hono route mounting is imperative and order/SmartRouter-sensitive; we need an explicit register step). But borrow the **composition discipline** and **immutability mindset**.

## 7. Design Synthesis — What SonicJS Should Borrow

| Decision | Source | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| **Imperative `register(app)` + async `onBoot`** two-phase lifecycle | Infowall v3 + Strapi register/bootstrap | Hono mounting is imperative & SmartRouter-sensitive; a functional transformer can't express "mount before the matcher builds." Two phases cleanly separate sync route mounting from async env-dependent wiring. |
| **Sync register at construction; async wire on first request** | Infowall v3 (empirical SmartRouter fix) | Avoids `Can not add a route since the matcher is already built`. SonicJS has the identical `/admin` catch-all structure and will hit the identical bug. |
| **A single shared `mountPlugin()` / `registerPluginRoutes()` primitive**, position-aware | Infowall §12 Q1; replaces hand-wiring in `app.ts` | Removes the 7+ hardcoded plugin mounts and the "MUST be before /admin/plugins" comments. |
| **Capability-gated context** (`ctx.email` throws `SonicCapabilityError` without `email:send`) | Infowall v3 | Real isolation boundary that Strapi/Payload lack. Phase 1 vocabulary: `email:send`, `hooks.*`, `db:*`, `cron:register`, `cache:*`, etc. |
| **Typed hook subscriptions** with narrowed payloads | Infowall v3 + Payload typed hooks | Replaces today's string-keyed, untyped hooks. TS rejects wrong field names at subscribe site. |
| **Singleton services** (three-fn API, throw-before-set) for env-independent access | Infowall v3 (`hook-system-singleton.ts` pattern already in repo) | Lets cron/`scheduled()` handlers get services without per-request env. |
| **Plugin cron declarations** dispatched by one `scheduled()` runner | Payload jobs + Infowall cron | Workers cron triggers fan out to plugins by `hookFamily`. |
| **`disable` keeps schema; only `uninstall` drops tables** | Payload `disabled`≠removed | Prevents destructive migrations on toggle. |
| **Namespacing (`plugin::<name>`)** for plugin-owned tables/services | Strapi | Avoids collisions; enables introspection. |
| **`package.json` metadata key for discovery** (build-time registry on Workers) | Strapi `strapi.kind` | Workers has no runtime `fs`; keep the build-time `generate-plugin-registry.mjs` but formalize it and document it (#621). |
| **Explicit `plugins.register: Plugin[]` consumer API** | PR #829 | The user-facing entry; carries forward #829 but corrected for the SmartRouter + `disableAll` issues. |
| **Zod-parsed DB rows** at the `PluginService` boundary | PR #834 | Typed shapes in/out of D1; no loose JSON. |

**What we deliberately reject:** Strapi's three interception layers; Payload's pure no-register functional model (incompatible with Hono mounting); runtime filesystem autoload (no `fs` on Workers).

## 8. Target Architecture — SonicJS v3 Plugin SDK

### 8.1 The plugin definition

```ts
// New: definePlugin() — the authoring entry point
export const emailPlugin = definePlugin({
  id: 'email',
  name: 'Email',
  version: '3.0.0',

  // Declared, validated capabilities. ctx is gated to exactly these.
  capabilities: ['email:send', 'hooks.auth:subscribe', 'cron:register', 'db:email_log'],

  // Plugin-owned tables (namespaced plugin::email_*). Created on install, dropped on uninstall ONLY.
  schema: [emailLogTable],

  // SYNC. Mounts routes. No async, no Promise. Throws if it returns one.
  register(app, ctx) {
    app.route('/admin/plugins/email', emailAdminRoutes)
    app.route('/api/email', emailApiRoutes)
  },

  // ASYNC. Runs on first request, after ALL plugins have registered.
  async onBoot(ctx) {
    const email = getEmailService()                 // singleton, env-independent
    ctx.hooks.on('auth:registration:completed', async (payload) => {
      // payload is the narrowed, typed shape — no casts
      await email.send(welcomeEmail(payload.user))
    })
  },

  // Cron declarations, dispatched by the single scheduled() runner.
  crons: [{ schedule: '*/15 * * * *', hookFamily: 'email-reconciliation' }],
  async onCronTick(event, ctx) {
    if (event.hookFamily !== 'email-reconciliation') return
    await reconcileDeliveries(getEmailService())
  },

  // Lifecycle (DB/schema only; never touches routes)
  async install(ctx)   { /* create plugin::email_* tables */ },
  async uninstall(ctx) { /* drop plugin::email_* tables */ },
  // activate/deactivate flip status ONLY — never create/drop schema (Payload lesson)
})
```

### 8.2 Two-phase boot (the heart of the fix)

```
createSonicJSApp(config)
        │
        ▼
  registerPluginRoutes(app, plugins)        ← SYNC, at construction
        │   • validate + topo-sort by dependsOn
        │   • app.route('/admin/logs', …)   (core mounts)
        │   • for each plugin: plugin.register(app, ctx)   ← routes mount here
        │   • app.route('/admin', adminUsers)  ← catch-all registers AFTER plugins
        ▼
  [ Hono SmartRouter matcher builds on first request — now safe ]
        │
        ▼
  First HTTP request
        │
        ▼
  wireRegisteredPlugins(ordered, byId, ctx)  ← ASYNC, lazy, once
            • ctx.hooks subscriptions
            • cron registration
            • plugin.onBoot(ctx)
```

**Contract enforced in code:**
- `register()` returning a `Promise` → throw `PluginRegisterMustBeSyncError`.
- Plugin routes always registered **between** core mounts and the `/admin` catch-all → no shadowing.
- `wireRegisteredPlugins` runs exactly once (guarded flag), lazily, so per-request `env` is available.

### 8.3 New / changed files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `plugins/sdk/define-plugin.ts` | `definePlugin()` — typed authoring entry. |
| `plugins/mount.ts` | `registerPluginRoutes(app, plugins)` + `mountPlugin()` shared primitive (carries #829 forward, SmartRouter-safe). |
| `plugins/wire.ts` | `wireRegisteredPlugins()` — hooks, crons, onBoot. |
| `plugins/capabilities.ts` | Capability vocabulary + `SonicCapabilityError` + `makePluginContext(caps)` gating. |
| `plugins/hooks/catalog.ts` | Typed hook event catalog (names → payload types). |
| `plugins/singletons/*-singleton.ts` | Service singletons (email, hooks, …) mirroring existing `hook-system-singleton.ts`. |
| `plugins/cron.ts` | Cron collector + `dispatchCronTick(event)` for the Workers `scheduled()` handler. |
| `services/plugin-service.ts` | Hardened with Zod row parsing (#834). |
| `app.ts` | Remove 7+ hardcoded plugin mounts; call `registerPluginRoutes()` once. |
| `config` (`SonicJSConfig`) | `plugins: { register: Plugin[]; disableAll?: boolean }`; deprecate `autoLoad`/`directory` no-ops (#829). |

### 8.4 Capability vocabulary (Phase 1)

`email:send` · `hooks.auth:subscribe` · `hooks.content:subscribe` · `cron:register` · `db:<table>` · `cache:read` · `cache:write` · `media:read` · `media:write` · `http:fetch` · `admin:menu`. (Payment/queue capabilities deferred to Phase 2 — matches Infowall §12 Q2's open question.)

### 8.5 Hook event catalog (typed, reconciled)

Reconcile the currently-declared events down to *dispatched* ones, typed. Content lifecycle (6, already firing) + auth events (`auth:registration:completed`, `auth:password-reset:requested`, `auth:password-reset:completed`). Each name maps to a payload interface; `ctx.hooks.on(name, handler)` infers the payload. **Action item:** audit declared-but-never-fired events and either fire or remove them (Infowall §12 Q3 — "ten events still declared-but-not-fired").

## 9. Phased Implementation Plan

Each phase is independently shippable and test-gated. **No phase merges without its tests green.**

### Phase 0 — Baseline & safety net (no behavior change)
- Add **integration + E2E tests that capture today's behavior** (which core plugin routes resolve, which 404). This is the regression guardrail.
- Land **#834** (Zod-parse `PluginService` rows) — pure hardening, no behavior change.
- **Exit:** full suite green; documented baseline of working vs. 404 plugin routes.

### Phase 1 — The mount primitive (fixes #758, #829, #621)
- Implement `plugins/mount.ts`: `registerPluginRoutes(app, plugins)` + `mountPlugin()`, **sync, position-aware**, inserted between core mounts and the `/admin` catch-all in `app.ts`.
- Add `plugins.register: Plugin[]` to `SonicJSConfig`; deprecate `autoLoad`/`directory` as documented no-ops.
- Enforce **`register()` must be sync** (reject Promise with named error).
- Remove the hand-wired plugin mounts from `app.ts` *one at a time*, replacing with `register()`.
- **Resolve #829's blocker:** define `disableAll` semantics explicitly — `disableAll` skips *core* plugin mounting; `register`-ed user plugins still mount unless individually disabled — and **make docs match code** (the @furelid review item). Add a test asserting the exact semantics.
- **Exit:** global-variables routes resolve (#758 closed); a custom plugin passed via `plugins.register` mounts with zero core edits; #829 unblocked; #621 docs updated.

### Phase 2 — Two-phase wiring + typed hooks
- Implement `wireRegisteredPlugins()` (`plugins/wire.ts`): lazy first-request, once-guarded; runs hook subscriptions + `onBoot`.
- Ship the **typed hook catalog** (`plugins/hooks/catalog.ts`); migrate the hook system to typed `on(name, handler)`.
- Keep the legacy `registerPlugins()` wrapper as a back-compat shim for existing tests.
- **Exit:** a plugin can subscribe to `auth:registration:completed` with a typed payload; wiring runs exactly once; legacy hook tests still pass.

### Phase 3 — Capabilities + singleton services
- Implement `plugins/capabilities.ts` + `makePluginContext()` gating; `SonicCapabilityError`.
- Introduce service singletons (email first) mirroring `hook-system-singleton.ts`.
- **Exit:** accessing `ctx.email` without `email:send` throws, caught by a unit test; cron-context (no request env) can still reach the singleton.

### Phase 4 — Cron surface
- `plugins/cron.ts`: collect `crons[]` from plugins; `dispatchCronTick(event)` wired into the Worker `scheduled()` handler; filter by `hookFamily`.
- **Exit:** a plugin's `onCronTick` fires on schedule in a Miniflare/integration test; graceful skip when credentials/bindings absent.

### Phase 5 — `definePlugin()` + Email reference migration (PR-E equivalent)
- **5a — `definePlugin()` ✅ DONE** (stacked branch `lane711/plugin-system-define`). See Appendix G.
- 5b — Migrate the **email plugin** as the reference (it touches capabilities, hooks, cron, singleton, routes — if it holds for email it holds for all). Close the `reset_link` leak; add `email_log` observability.
- 5c — Fix **magic-link** (`c.env.plugins?.get('email')` → `getEmailService().send()`).
- 5d — Add real `dispatch()` sites in content/auth routes (this *activates* the now-subscribed core plugin hooks; behavior-changing — needs dedicated integration tests).
- **Exit:** email plugin runs fully on v3; documented as the template for the rest.

### Phase 6 — Migrate remaining core plugins (~20)
- Mechanically migrate each core plugin to `definePlugin()` using email as the template. Batch by risk: leaf plugins (hello-world, code-examples, testimonials) first; auth-adjacent (otp, oauth, user-profiles) and stateful (stripe, ai-search, analytics, workflow) last.
- Delete the corresponding hand-wired blocks from `app.ts` as each lands.
- **Exit:** `app.ts` has **zero** hardcoded plugin mounts; all plugins flow through `registerPluginRoutes()`.

### Phase 7 — Docs, DX, and acceptance plugins
- Plugin development guide (#359), registry-generation docs (#621), FAQ/field-types accuracy (#471).
- Build **two greenfield acceptance plugins** to prove the contract end-to-end: **MCP plugin (#784)** and **Web Monitor (#577, exercises cron + services + http:fetch)**.
- **Exit:** a third party can author + register a plugin using only public docs, no core edits.

### Phase 8 — Marketplace foundation (downstream, optional)
- With a stable contract, tackle #360 (registry/discovery/versioning) then #367 (ratings). Out of scope for the "fix it once and for all" core effort but unblocked by it.

## 10. Testing Strategy

> **Principle:** the area that is broken today (generic mounting + wiring) is the area with no tests. Every phase ships unit **and** integration **and** (where user-visible) E2E coverage. Target: no plugin behavior is "verified" by manual clicking.

### 10.1 Unit tests (`packages/core/src/__tests__/plugins/`, Vitest)

| Area | Cases |
|---|---|
| `mount.ts` | route mounting; multi-route plugin; **position** (plugin routes register before `/admin` catch-all); priority ordering; empty-plugin no-op; **`register()` returning a Promise throws**; topo-sort by `dependsOn`; circular-dep error. |
| `capabilities.ts` | `ctx.email` throws `SonicCapabilityError` without `email:send`; allowed capability resolves; unknown capability rejected at validate. |
| typed hooks | `on('auth:registration:completed', …)` infers payload; wrong field name is a *type* error (type-level test via `tsd`/`expect-type`); priority ordering; cancellation; scoped `unregisterAll` on deactivate. |
| singletons | throw-before-set; set-once; same instance across calls. |
| cron | collector aggregates `crons[]`; `dispatchCronTick` filters by `hookFamily`; graceful skip on missing binding. |
| `plugin-service.ts` (#834) | Zod parse of plugin/stats/activity/hook/route rows; numeric coercion; **invalid settings payload rejected**; structured activity details. |
| `disableAll` semantics | exact matrix: core off + user on; per-plugin disable; docs-match assertion. |

### 10.2 Integration tests (in-process app via `createSonicJSApp`, Miniflare D1)

| Area | Cases |
|---|---|
| End-to-end mount | `createSonicJSApp({ plugins: { register: [testPlugin] } })` → `GET` the plugin route returns 200 (the #758 regression test). |
| global-variables | activate → `GET /api/global-variables` 200, `GET /admin/global-variables` 200, menu item present (the literal #758 repro). |
| Two-phase wiring | `onBoot` runs once on first request; hook fires with real payload against **real D1**, not mocks. |
| Lifecycle | install creates `plugin::*` tables; **deactivate does NOT drop tables**; uninstall drops them (Payload lesson, asserted). |
| Cron | scheduled tick dispatches to the right plugin; reconciliation writes back to `email_log`. |
| Capability denial | a plugin without `email:send` getting `ctx.email` surfaces `SonicCapabilityError` through the request path. |
| Dependency order | plugin B depending on A boots after A; missing dependency errors clearly. |

### 10.3 E2E tests (Playwright, `tests/e2e/`)

Extend the existing specs (`15-plugins`, `29-email-plugin-settings`, `43-cache-plugin`, …) and add:

| Spec | Flow |
|---|---|
| plugin mount E2E | Activate global-variables in admin → navigate to its admin page → renders (not 404). |
| email reference | Configure email settings → test-send → result feedback → `email_log` browser shows the entry. |
| activate/deactivate safety | Deactivate a plugin → its routes 404/redirect, **its data survives**; reactivate → data intact. |
| custom plugin smoke | Starter template + a custom `register`-ed plugin in dev → route reachable (the Infowall "visual smoke test" item). |
| settings activity | Save plugin settings → Activity tab renders a readable entry (carries #834's Playwright spec forward). |

### 10.4 CI gates
- `npm run type-check` (core) + `tsc --noEmit` clean.
- Vitest unit + integration green (no net-new skips — note #414: 84% of E2E currently skipped; new specs must actually run).
- Type-level tests for hook payload inference.
- Playwright suite green for touched specs; D1 migration timing fixed for plugin specs (relates to #607).

## 11. Core Plugin Migration Plan

~22 core plugins under `plugins/core-plugins/`. Migrate to `definePlugin()` in risk order, deleting the matching `app.ts` hand-wire as each lands.

| Batch | Plugins | Why this order |
|---|---|---|
| **Reference** | `email-plugin` | Touches every SDK surface; the template (Phase 5). |
| **Leaf / low-risk** | `hello-world-plugin`, `code-examples`, `testimonials`, `quill-editor`, `shortcodes-plugin`, `global-variables-plugin` | No env-dependent services; global-variables/shortcodes also close #758/#756. |
| **Auth-adjacent** | `otp-login-plugin`, `oauth-providers`, `user-profiles`, `magic-link` (available), `security-audit-plugin`, `turnstile-plugin` | Share auth hooks; magic-link fix folds in. |
| **Stateful / external** | `stripe-plugin`, `ai-search-plugin`, `analytics`, `workflow-plugin`, `cache`, `redirect-management`, `media`, `database-tools-plugin`, `seed-data-plugin`, `demo-login` | Bindings, crons, external APIs — highest blast radius; do last with full integration coverage. |

**Per-plugin checklist:** declare capabilities → move route mounting into sync `register()` → move service wiring into async `onBoot()` → convert hooks to typed `on()` → declare `crons` if any → install/uninstall create/drop only plugin-owned tables → delete `app.ts` hand-wire → add/port unit + integration + E2E.

| **#577** Web Monitor plugin | Phase 7 | Greenfield acceptance plugin exercising cron + services. |
| **#471** FAQ/field-types docs | Phase 7 | Folded into docs pass. |
| **#360 / #367** marketplace | Phase 8 | Unblocked by a stable contract; out of core scope. |
| **#607 / #414** E2E/test-debt | Phase 0 + CI gates | New specs must actually run (no silent skips); fix D1 migration timing for plugin specs. |

## 13. Risks & Open Questions

**Risks**
- **Hono SmartRouter lock** — the central technical risk; mitigated by the sync-register design (§8.2) and an explicit "register returning a Promise throws" guard + test.
- **Big-bang `app.ts` edits** — mitigated by removing hand-wires one plugin at a time, each behind a passing integration test (Phase 6).
- **Workers has no runtime `fs`** — no directory autoload; discovery stays build-time (`generate-plugin-registry.mjs`), which must be documented (#621) and ideally validated in CI.
- **Destructive migrations on toggle** — mitigated by the Payload rule: activate/deactivate never touch schema; only install/uninstall do (asserted in integration tests).
- **E2E skip debt (#414)** — new specs must run, not skip; otherwise the guardrail is illusory.

**Open questions (to settle before/early in Phase 1)**
1. **`mountPlugin()` ownership** — does the shared mount primitive live in `@sonicjs-cms/core` only, or is it designed to be reused by forks (Infowall)? (Infowall §12 Q1.) Recommendation: core, exported.
2. **Capability vocabulary scope** — are payment/queue/scheduled-fetch capabilities Phase 1 or Phase 2? (Infowall §12 Q2.) Recommendation: Phase 2.
3. **Hook event reconciliation** — which of the ten declared-but-never-fired events do we fire vs. delete? Align names *now* to avoid divergent vocabularies. (Infowall §12 Q3 — highest-value alignment item.)
4. **Legacy hook adapter lifetime** — keep the v1→v3 adapter until the last plugin migrates (end of Phase 6), then remove. (Infowall §12 Q4.)
5. **`disableAll` exact semantics** — **DECIDED (Phase 1):** `disableAll: true` disables *all* plugins — core **and** user `register`-ed. No plugin routes are mounted and plugin bootstrap (DB seeding) is skipped; only the core CMS routes remain. Rationale: matches the original in-code intent ("Disable all plugins including core plugins"), matches `bootstrapMiddleware` which already skipped plugin bootstrap on `disableAll`, and is the simplest mental model. Code and docs now agree (resolves the @furelid review mismatch). Encoded in `mount-integration.test.ts`.

- `packages/core/src/plugins/mount.ts` — `registerPluginRoutes()` + `mountPlugin()` + `PluginRegisterMustBeSyncError`. Sync, priority-ordered, duplicate-path warnings, structural `MountablePlugin` contract (sidesteps the `src` vs `dist` `Plugin` identity clash).
- `Plugin.register?(app)` added to `plugins/types.ts` (sync-only, documented).

- `app.ts`: the 7 hand-wired `if (plugin.routes) { for … app.route() }` blocks replaced by two `registerPluginRoutes()` calls; **`globalVariablesPlugin` + `shortcodesPlugin` now mounted (fixes #758)**; user `plugins.register` plugins mounted before the `/admin` catch-all (#829, #621); all plugin mounting gated by `disableAll`.

## Appendix C — Phase 2 status (foundation implemented)

**Finding:** hooks were *dead metadata at runtime* — `HookSystemImpl` is only instantiated inside `PluginManager`, which is never instantiated in the running app, and no route dispatches lifecycle events. Same disease as routes pre-Phase 1. (Subscribing plugin hooks is therefore inert until dispatch sites are added — which makes activating the wiring safe.)

**Landed (the typed-hook + two-phase-wiring foundation):**
- `plugins/hooks/catalog.ts` — typed event catalog (6 content + 3 auth events) → payload types; `HookEventName`, `HookPayload<E>`, runtime `HOOK_EVENT_NAMES` + `isKnownHookEvent()`.
- `plugins/hooks/typed-hooks.ts` — `createTypedHooks(hookSystem)` → `{ on<E>, dispatch<E> }` with catalog inference; structural `HookSystemLike` (both `HookSystemImpl` and `ScopedHookSystem` satisfy it).
- `plugins/hooks/hook-system-singleton.ts` — `get/set/has/resetHookSystem()` + `getTypedHooks()`. Throw-before-get; idempotent set (multi-app/test safe); `reset` for isolation. Gives env-independent access for cron (Phase 4).
- `plugins/wire.ts` — `wireRegisteredPlugins(plugins, ctx)`: subscribe ALL plugin `hooks[]` first, then run each `onBoot` (per-plugin error isolation); structural `WirablePlugin` with async `onBoot`. `createPluginWirer()` once-guard for the lazy first-request trigger.
- Exported the whole surface from `plugins/index.ts`.

**Tests:** `typed-hooks.test.ts` (11 runtime + a `tsc`-validated type-level block proving narrowed payloads and rejected unknown events/fields) and `wire.test.ts` (8: subscribe→dispatch, onBoot ordering "all hooks before any onBoot", error isolation, once-guard runs exactly once under concurrency, lazy list eval). Full core suite **1517 passed, 0 failed**; `tsc` clean.

## Appendix D — Phase 2b status (wiring activated in the live app)

**Landed:** the wiring foundation is now active in `createSonicJSApp`:
- Eager `setHookSystem(new HookSystemImpl())` at construction — the singleton is published before anything else.
- Core plugins extracted into shared `corePluginsBeforeCatchAll` / `corePluginsAfterCatchAll` arrays, reused for **both** route mounting and wiring so the two never drift (annotations dropped to dodge the `src`/`dist` `Plugin` identity clash; both consumers are structural).
- A once-guarded first-request middleware (after bootstrap) runs `wireRegisteredPlugins` exactly once: subscribes every core + user plugin's `hooks[]` to the app hook system and runs their `onBoot`. Error-isolated (never breaks a request) and skipped entirely under `disableAll`.

**Effect:** the hook system is now genuinely live — the first request subscribes the real core plugin hooks (`request:start`, `content:read` ×2 from global-variables/shortcodes, `user:login`, …). These remain **inert until dispatch sites are added**, so no existing behavior changes; the infrastructure is proven working end-to-end.

**Tests:** `wire-integration.test.ts` (4): singleton published at construction; first request runs `onBoot` + subscribes hooks (verified by dispatching `content:create` and seeing the handler fire); wires exactly once across 3 requests; `disableAll` skips wiring. Full core suite **1521 passed, 0 failed**; `tsc` clean.

**Next (Phase 5 / dispatch sites):** add real `dispatch()` calls in content/auth routes and migrate the email plugin to subscribe `auth:registration:completed` — the point at which wiring becomes user-visible (and where the `reset_link` leak / `email_log` work lands). Deferred here because it changes behavior and belongs with the email reference migration.

## Appendix E — Phase 3 status (capabilities + service singletons)

**Landed (pure infrastructure, no behavior change):**

**Tests:** `capabilities.test.ts` (19): vocabulary incl. `db:<table>` pattern matching, granted/denied gating (throws `SonicCapabilityError` with the right `.capability`/`.plugin`), `cache` accepting read-or-write, lazy provider invocation, and the service-singleton contract (throw-before-get, idempotent set, cron-reachable without env, slot independence). Full core suite **1540 passed, 0 failed**; `tsc` clean.

**Wiring into the live app** (providing real `email`/`cache`/`http` providers + passing the gated context to plugins) lands with `definePlugin()` in Phase 5, where plugins actually declare `capabilities` and consume `ctx`.

## Appendix F — Phase 4 status (cron surface)

Built on the stacked branch `lane711/plugin-system-cron` (PR base = the foundation branch / #841).

**Landed (infrastructure; no consumer change yet):**
- `plugins/cron.ts` — `CronDeclaration` (`{ schedule, hookFamily }`) + structural `CronablePlugin` (`crons[]` + async `onCronTick`). `collectCrons()` / `collectCronSchedules()` flatten declarations (for wrangler sync + diagnostics). `dispatchCronTick(plugins, cron, scheduledTime, ctx)` fans a fired expression out to matching plugins, tagging each `onCronTick` with the matched `hookFamily`, one call per matching declaration, error-isolated. `createScheduledHandler({ plugins, getHooks, disabled })` returns a Cloudflare `scheduled(controller, env, ctx)` handler that reaches services via the **env-independent singletons** (cron has no `c.env`), passes the Worker `env` into the cron context, and `waitUntil`s the work.
- Exported from `plugins/index.ts`.

**Design note (matches Payload jobs):** declaring a `schedule` runs nothing by itself — the execution mechanism is the Cloudflare Cron Trigger delivered to `scheduled()`. The consumer still lists the expressions in `wrangler.toml [triggers]`; the plugin `crons[]` are the source of truth for which plugin owns which expression (`collectCronSchedules()` can generate the wrangler list).

**Tests:** `cron.test.ts` (12): collect/flatten + malformed-entry skipping, dispatch matches only the fired cron, well-formed event, unmatched reporting, multi-cron fan-out (one call per declaration), error isolation, and the `scheduled` handler (dispatch + `waitUntil` + env passthrough + lazy list + `disabled` no-op). Full core suite **1552 passed, 0 failed**; `tsc` clean.

**Deferred:** wiring `scheduled` into the consumer Worker export (`export default { fetch, scheduled }`) + the starter template + `wrangler.toml` trigger generation — a DX change bundled with `definePlugin()`/docs (Phase 5/7), since it changes how consumers export their Worker.

## Appendix G — Phase 5a status (`definePlugin()`)

Built on the stacked branch `lane711/plugin-system-define` (PR base = the cron branch). Purely additive authoring API — no behavior change; nothing yet *uses* it in core.

**Landed:**
- `plugins/sdk/define-plugin.ts` — `definePlugin(input)` returns a unified `DefinedPlugin` that structurally satisfies `MountablePlugin` (routes/register), `WirablePlugin` (onBoot), and `CronablePlugin` (crons/onCronTick), plus the legacy metadata fields the admin/registry read. Normalizes `id → name`; validates declared `capabilities` (warns on unknown); tags output with `__sonicV3` (+ `isDefinedPlugin()` guard).
- **Enriched context:** the author's `onBoot`/`onCronTick` receive `{ hooks, cap, env, raw }` — a *typed* hook facade (`ctx.hooks.on('auth:registration:completed', …)` with narrowed payloads) and the *capability-gated* service context (`ctx.cap.email` throws `SonicCapabilityError` without `email:send`). `definePlugin` wraps the author functions so the runtime keeps passing the plain `PluginBootContext`/`CronContext`; providers ride on `raw.providers` (host-supplied).
- Exported from `plugins/index.ts`.

**Tests:** `define-plugin.test.ts` (13: shape/normalization, id/version required, unknown-capability warning, mounts via `registerPluginRoutes`, typed-hook subscription fires through the live system, capability gating throws, provider resolution, env exposure, cron enriched context) + `define-plugin-integration.test.ts` (3: mounts through `createSonicJSApp`, honors `disableAll`, `onBoot` runs exactly once on first request via live wiring). Full core suite **1565 passed, 0 failed**; `tsc` clean.

**Next (5b–5d):** migrate the email plugin onto `definePlugin` (capabilities + `onBoot` hook subscriptions + `email_log` + reconciliation cron, closing the `reset_link` leak), fix magic-link, and add the content/auth `dispatch()` sites — all behavior-changing, each with its own integration coverage.

## Appendix H — Phase 5b status (provider-agnostic email + leak fix)

Same stacked branch. **Decision (from product):** developers must be able to use *any* email provider, and every send must be recorded.

**5b-1 — EmailService core (additive):**
- `services/email`: `EmailProvider` interface + built-in **Resend / SendGrid / Console** providers; a dev can pass any `EmailProvider`. `EmailService.send()` normalizes → sends → records to `email_log` (best-effort; logging never fails a send; a throwing provider becomes a structured failure).
- `resolveEmailProvider` precedence: explicit instance > named built-in > env auto-detect (`RESEND_API_KEY`, then `SENDGRID_API_KEY`) > Console. An unconfigured choice **degrades to Console with a warning** — a missing key becomes "logged, not delivered", never a silent token leak.
- `email-service` singleton (env-independent, for cron reconciliation). Core `email_log` table: Drizzle schema + **migration 037** (bundled), with `failed_at_send` / `delivery_state` / `delivery_synced_at` for reconciliation.
- Tests: `email-service.test.ts` (19).

**5b-2 — wiring + call-site migration (behavior-changing):**
- `app.ts`: `email` config (`{ provider | providerName | from }`); first request resolves the provider and publishes the EmailService singleton (isolated init — can't block plugin wiring); `ctx.cap.email` now resolves to it.
- **SECURITY FIX:** `POST /auth/request-password-reset` no longer returns `reset_link` in the JSON response (it leaked a valid reset token to any caller). It now **emails** the link (`flow: 'password-reset'`) and returns only the generic enumeration-safe message.
- magic-link: replaced the broken `c.env.plugins?.get('email')` registry lookup (links were only console-logged) with `getEmailService().send({ flow: 'magic-link' })`.
- Tests: `email-wiring-integration.test.ts` (3) through the real app — provider initialized on first request; reset omits `reset_link` + the token and sends instead; unknown email stays generic and sends nothing.

Full core suite **1587 passed, 0 failed**; `tsc` clean.

**Verified findings (from the requested audit):** transport was fractured (Resend hardcoded in OTP, SendGrid in email-templates, broken registry in magic-link); `email_log` existed only in the optional email-templates-plugin; the reset link **was** leaked in the API response. All three are now addressed except the OTP migration (works today via Resend; deferred to limit blast radius).

**Still deferred (5c/5d):** migrate the email *plugin* itself onto `definePlugin` with a reconciliation cron; OTP → shared EmailService; content/auth `dispatch()` sites that activate the now-subscribed hooks; an `email_log` admin browser.

# Wire tenant.ts → auth_tenant

# Wire tenant.ts → auth_tenant

Flip tenant registry source of truth from document-backed (`type_id='tenant'` rows) to the
Better Auth `auth_tenant` table (organization plugin). Greenfield only.

## Changes

1. **`0001_core.sql`** — add `status` / `domain` / `notes` columns to `auth_tenant` + domain index.
2. **`db/schema.ts`** — mirror new columns on `authTenant`.
3. **`auth/config.ts`** — `organization()` schema `additionalFields` for status/domain/notes so BA-native flows round-trip them.
4. **`TenantService`** — keep public API identical; swap storage `documents` → `auth_tenant`. Timestamps in **ms** (auth-table convention). `countDocumentsForTenant` still queries `documents.tenant_id` (content ownership unchanged).
5. **`middleware/tenant.ts`** — `loadTenantState()` reads `auth_tenant` instead of `type_id='tenant'` docs. Plugin-active gate unchanged (still doc-backed plugin registry).
6. **`tenant-service.sqlite.test.ts`** — assert against `auth_tenant` rows, drop `registerTenantType`.

## Not in scope (follow-ups)

- **Membership gate** — `auth_tenant_member` lookup in `resolveTenantSlug`/switcher so a user can only
  switch to tenants they belong to. (Security win; needs per-request user context.)
- Remove dead `tenant` document type + `q_tenant_*` generated columns from `document-types-seed.ts`.

## Review

Shipped. Tenant registry source of truth flipped documents → `auth_tenant`.

- `0001_core.sql`: `auth_tenant` gains `status`/`domain`/`notes` + `idx_auth_tenant_domain`. Bundle regen'd, app copy synced byte-identical (R9).
- `db/schema.ts`: `authTenant` mirrors columns.
- `auth/config.ts`: `organization()` schema `additionalFields` for the 3 fields.
- `TenantService`: internals → `auth_tenant` (raw SQL), public API unchanged → admin routes untouched. ms timestamps. `countDocumentsForTenant` still reads `documents.tenant_id`.
- `middleware/tenant.ts`: `loadTenantState()` reads `auth_tenant`.
- `tenant-service.sqlite.test.ts`: rewritten to assert `auth_tenant`.

Verification: `tsc` clean · 23 plugin unit tests pass · spec 70 (6 tests) pass · local D1 reset + reseeded.

Dead but harmless (cleanup follow-up): `tenant` document type + `q_tenant_status`/`q_tenant_domain`
generated columns still registered in `document-types-seed.ts` — no longer read.

### Membership gate (security) — SHIPPED
`auth_tenant_member` now gates tenant access for authed requests.

- `TenantService`: `listMemberSlugs` / `isMember` (default always allowed) / `addMember` (idempotent, `INSERT OR IGNORE`).
- `resolveTenantSlug(state, req, { memberSlugs, enforceMembership })`: when enforcing, every non-'default'
  candidate (header/cookie/domain/subdomain) must be in `memberSlugs`, else falls through → 'default'. No leak.
- `tenantMiddleware`: enforces only when `c.get('user')` present + plugin active (runs after session mw at app.ts:445).
  Anonymous/public requests stay ungated → public multi-tenant API/content serving unchanged.
- Switcher POST `/admin/tenants/switch`: 403 if not a member.
- Create route auto-enrolls the creator as `owner` (so they can immediately switch in — and so spec 70 stays green).
- Sidebar switcher dropdown filtered to member tenants.

Verification: `tsc` clean · 32 unit tests (resolver gate + membership CRUD) · spec 71 (5 tests) + spec 70 (6 tests) green.

### Deferred
- Remove dead `tenant` document type + `q_tenant_*` generated columns from `document-types-seed.ts`.

# Phase 2: per-tenant roles (G1) + super-admin (G2)

## Locked model
- Role/verb/grant **definitions** stay global (rbac_role/verb docs under 'default') — one platform role catalog.
- Role **assignment** is per-tenant:
  - `default` tenant → global `rbac_user_roles` doc (unchanged, back-compat).
  - tenant T ≠ default → `auth_tenant_member.role` holds the rbac role **name** the user has in T.
- `can(userId, resource, verb, tenantId)` resolves grants from the per-tenant role when T≠default, else global.
- **Super-admin (G2)** = explicit `auth_user.is_super_admin` flag (default 0). Bypasses membership gate +
  uses global roles in every tenant. NOT derived from the 'admin' role (admin's `*:manage` wildcard would
  make every admin a super-admin and re-open the gate). Opt-in only.

## G2 (super-admin) — build first (bounded)
1. `auth_user.is_super_admin INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` (migration + schema + BA user additionalField input:false).
2. `app.ts`: carry `isSuperAdmin` on `c.get('user')` from BA session.user (no extra query).
3. `tenant.ts`: `enforceMembership = userPresent && pluginActive && !isSuperAdmin`.
4. switcher POST: bypass membership if super-admin.
5. Tests: e2e — super-admin switches into a non-member tenant (extends spec 71).

## G1 (per-tenant roles) — SHIPPED
Two-layer authorization (clean separation, no RBAC-core signature churn):
- **Global role** gates route *access* (`requireRole`/`requireRbac`) — can you enter the admin doc
  routes / platform sections at all. Unchanged.
- **Per-tenant role** gates the document *operation* (document ACL `baseGrants[role]`) — what you can
  do with content in the active tenant.

Implementation:
- `auth_tenant_member.role` holds a role name the document ACL understands (admin/editor/author/viewer).
  Tenant creator auto-enrolls as `admin` (was `owner`).
- `TenantService.listMemberRoles` / `getMemberRole`.
- `tenant.ts`: resolves the user's role in the active tenant onto `c.set('tenantRole')`
  (global role for 'default' / super-admins).
- `getDocumentRequestContext` (the single ACL coupling point) feeds `tenantRole` as the role principal —
  so the same user is admin in one tenant, viewer in another.

Verification: `tsc` clean · 32 MT unit tests (incl. per-tenant role CRUD) · e2e spec 72
(viewer-in-tenant denied create / allowed read / global admin create in default) · specs 70+71 green.

## G4 (member management UI) — SHIPPED
`/admin/tenants/<slug>/members` — add a user by email with a per-tenant role, change role inline,
remove. Lockout guards refuse demoting/removing the last admin.

- `TenantService`: `listMembers` (joined w/ auth_user), `addMemberByEmail`, `setMemberRole`,
  `removeMember`, `adminCount`; `VALID_MEMBER_ROLES` = admin/editor/author/viewer.
- Routes: GET/POST `/:slug/members`, POST `/:slug/members/:userId/role`, `/:slug/members/:userId/delete`.
- `tenant-members.template.ts` + a "Members" action on each tenant row.

Verification: `tsc` clean · 33 MT unit tests (incl. lockout guards) · e2e spec 73 (add/role/remove +
error) · specs 70/71/72 green.

## G3 (invitation flow) — SHIPPED
Invite an email to a tenant with a per-tenant role; the invitee joins by opening the accept link
while signed in with the invited email. On the members page (`/admin/tenants/<slug>/members`).

- `TenantService`: `createInvitation` (pending row, id = accept token, 7-day TTL), `listInvitations`,
  `revokeInvitation`, `acceptInvitation` (fail-closed: pending + non-expired + signed-in email must
  match the invited email — never token-only).
- Routes: POST `/:slug/invitations`, POST `/:slug/invitations/:id/revoke`, and
  GET `/invitations/accept?token=…` (registered before `/:slug` routes; `invitations` is a reserved slug).
- Invitations section on the members template (invite form + pending list w/ accept link + revoke).

Verification: `tsc` clean · 34 MT unit tests (full lifecycle + email-mismatch/expiry/duplicate/revoke
guards) · e2e spec 74 (invite→accept→member, revoke) · specs 70–73 green.

## Email delivery — SHIPPED
Invitation accept link emailed via the app `EmailService` (best-effort, guarded by
`hasEmailService()`; link still shown in UI). Merged to v3 (PR #878).

## G5 (shared/global collections) — STARTED (foundation + vertical slice)
Centralized-first, safe-by-default approach.

- **Primitive (centralized decision):** `settings.global?: boolean` on document types +
  `GLOBAL_TENANT = '__global__'` + `effectiveTenantForType(requestTenant, settings)` in
  `document-request-context.ts`. Defaults to the request tenant → a type is isolated unless it opts
  into `global: true`, so **no existing type can regress into a cross-tenant leak**.
- **Wired (vertical slice):** `admin-documents` create + list — global types write to / read from the
  shared pool from any tenant.
- **Tests:** helper unit + `global-tenant-scope.sqlite.test.ts` (global visible from every tenant;
  normal type stays isolated — the security property).

### G5 — canonical document routes COMPLETE
Both R4-sanctioned document-model routes are now fully global-aware:
- `admin-documents`: create, list, get-by-id, versions, update, publish, unpublish, delete, reindex.
  By-id/root-id ops use `resolveDocScope` — look up the type without a tenant filter, compute the
  effective tenant, then **re-verify the row lives in that effective scope** (the isolation guard
  reproduces the old `AND tenant_id = ?` semantics for normal types → no leak).
- `api-documents`: list + by-id/by-root public reads. The ACL override lookup also uses the effective
  tenant (`denyIfNotAllowed`/`aclAllowsRead` take an override); the role principal stays per-tenant.

Proven end-to-end: e2e spec 75 (global type created in tenant A, visible from tenant B; normal type
isolated). 36 MT unit + 25 e2e green.

### G5 remaining (follow-up)
- Legacy `admin-content` / `api-content-crud` / `admin-media` / `media-documents` raw-SQL paths are
  NOT global-aware. These are the legacy content/media routes already slated for decommissioning
  (CLAUDE.md §"content/media table DROP") — global types are a document-model feature served by the
  document routes above, so this is intentional, not a silent gap.
- A way to mark a type global from config/UI (today: only via type registration `settings.global`).

## User- & role-centric membership UI — SHIPPED
Payload's model: one shared role catalog; global-vs-tenant is the *assignment location*
(global = `rbac_user_roles`/`is_super_admin`, per-tenant = `auth_tenant_member`). No schema change.

- **User-centric** (`/admin/tenants/users/:userId`): list a user's tenants + per-tenant role, add the
  user to a tenant (picker + role), change role, remove. Linked from the user edit page (`/admin/users/:id/edit`)
  when the plugin is active, and from each tenant member row ("All tenants").
- **Role-centric** (`/admin/tenants/roles/:roleName`, read-only): per-tenant assignments of a role.
  Linked per-role from the RBAC roles tab.
- `TenantService.listUserMemberships` / `listAssignmentsByRole`; reserved slugs `users`/`roles`.

Verification: 37 MT unit (incl. the two new queries) + e2e spec 76 (user edit link → add/change/remove +
role-usage page). Full suite 70–76 = 29 e2e green.

### Other deferred
- Optionally make `requireRbac` portal-section gates tenant-aware if any section should be per-tenant.
- The per-role "tenants" link on the RBAC roles tab is authored but not e2e-covered (hidden-tab DOM
  assertion was flaky); the role-usage page is reached directly + from user pages.

# Publishing Guide

Source: https://github.com/sonicjs-org/sonicjs/blob/main/PUBLISHING.md

# Publishing Guide

This guide explains how to publish new versions of SonicJS packages to npm.

## Prerequisites

1. You must be logged into npm with publish permissions:
   ```bash
   npm login
   ```

2. Verify you're logged in:
   ```bash
   npm whoami
   ```

3. Ensure all tests pass:
   ```bash
   npm test
   npm run e2e
   ```

## Quick Publishing

### Patch Release (Bug fixes - 2.0.4 → 2.0.5)
```bash
npm run release:patch
```

### Minor Release (New features - 2.0.4 → 2.1.0)
```bash
npm run release:minor
```

### Major Release (Breaking changes - 2.0.4 → 3.0.0)
```bash
npm run release:major
```

## What These Commands Do

Each `release:*` command automatically:
1. ✅ Bumps the version in `packages/core/package.json`
2. ✅ Updates the core version reference in `packages/create-app/src/cli.js`
3. ✅ Bumps the version in `packages/create-app/package.json`
4. ✅ Builds the core package
5. ✅ Publishes `@sonicjs-cms/core` to npm
6. ✅ Publishes `create-sonicjs` to npm

## Manual Publishing (Step by Step)

If you prefer more control, you can publish manually:

### 1. Bump the version
```bash
# For patch release (2.0.4 → 2.0.5)
npm run version:patch

# For minor release (2.0.4 → 2.1.0)
npm run version:minor

# For major release (2.0.4 → 3.0.0)
npm run version:major
```

This updates versions in:
- `packages/core/package.json`
- `packages/create-app/package.json`
- `packages/create-app/src/cli.js` (the core version used by create-sonicjs)

### 2. Review the changes
```bash
git diff
```

### 3. Commit the version bump
```bash
git add .
git commit -m "chore: release v2.0.5"
```

### 4. Publish to npm
```bash
# Publish both packages
npm run publish:all

# Or publish individually:
npm run publish:core        # Publishes @sonicjs-cms/core
npm run publish:create-app  # Publishes create-sonicjs
```

### 5. Create a git tag
```bash
# Use the version from packages/core/package.json
git tag v2.0.5
```

### 6. Push changes and tags
```bash
git push
git push --tags
```

## Package Versions

The monorepo maintains two npm packages:

- **@sonicjs-cms/core**: The core framework package
- **create-sonicjs**: The CLI tool for scaffolding new apps

When you bump the core version, the `sync-versions.js` script automatically:
- Updates the create-app CLI to install the new core version
- Bumps the create-sonicjs package version

## Version Synchronization

The `create-sonicjs` CLI hardcodes which version of `@sonicjs-cms/core` to install.
This is located at `packages/create-app/src/cli.js` line ~385:

```javascript
packageJson.dependencies = {
  '@sonicjs-cms/core': '^2.0.4',  // This gets auto-updated
  ...packageJson.dependencies
}
```

The `sync-versions.js` script keeps this in sync with the actual core version.

## Troubleshooting

### "You do not have permission to publish"
Run `npm login` and ensure you're authenticated with an account that has publish permissions.

### "Version already published"
You need to bump the version first. Run one of the `npm run version:*` commands.

### "No .npmrc file found"
Make sure you're in the repository root directory.

### Testing Locally Before Publishing

You can test the packages locally using npm link:

```bash
# In packages/core
cd packages/core
npm run build
npm link

# In your test app
cd /path/to/test-app
npm link @sonicjs-cms/core
```

### Publishing Beta Versions

To publish a beta version:

1. Manually set the version with a beta suffix:
   ```bash
   cd packages/core
   npm version 2.1.0-beta.1 --no-git-tag-version
   node ../../scripts/sync-versions.js
   ```

2. Publish with the beta tag:
   ```bash
   npm publish --workspace=@sonicjs-cms/core --tag beta
   npm publish --workspace=create-sonicjs --tag beta
   ```

3. Users can install with:
   ```bash
   npm create sonicjs@beta
   # or
   npm install @sonicjs-cms/core@beta
   ```

## After Publishing

1. **Verify on npm**: Check that packages are published:
   - https://www.npmjs.com/package/@sonicjs-cms/core
   - https://www.npmjs.com/package/create-sonicjs

2. **Test the CLI**: Try creating a new app:
   ```bash
   npm create sonicjs@latest my-test-app
   cd my-test-app
   npm install
   npm run dev
   ```

3. **Update documentation**: If there are breaking changes or new features, update:
   - README.md
   - CHANGELOG.md
   - Documentation site (www/)

4. **Create GitHub Release**: Create a release on GitHub with release notes:
   ```
   Title: v2.0.5
   Description: Bug fixes and improvements
   - Fixed database tools row click redirect issue
   - Added authentication middleware to database routes
   - Improved E2E test coverage
   ```

## CI/CD Integration (Future)

Consider setting up GitHub Actions to automate publishing:

```yaml
name: Publish to npm
on:
  push:
    tags:
      - 'v*'
jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v3
        with:
          node-version: '18'
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm run publish:all
        env:
          NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
```
